subject: Physics
topic: Motion — kinematics, acceleration, equations of motion

questions.stem: A car accelerates uniformly from rest with acceleration 2 m/s². What is its velocity after 5 seconds?
questions.explanation: v = u + at. u = 0 (rest), a = 2 m/s², t = 5 s. v = 0 + 2×5 = 10 m/s. Answer: B. Trap: confusing with distance or other formulas.

questions.stem: An object is thrown upward with initial velocity 20 m/s. What is the maximum height reached? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: At max height, v = 0. v² = u² - 2gh (upward, g opposes). 0 = 400 - 2×10×h. h = 400/20 = 20 m. Answer: C. Trap: forgetting negative acceleration or misapplying formula.

questions.stem: A particle moves with constant acceleration. If it travels 15 m in the first second and 25 m in the next second, what is the acceleration?
questions.explanation: Distance in successive seconds differs by acceleration. 25 - 15 = 10 m (represents acceleration effect). For constant acceleration, a = Δ(distance in consecutive intervals). a = 10 m/s². Answer: B. Trap: confusing displacement with velocity.

questions.stem: An object falls freely from rest for 2 seconds. What is the distance fallen? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½gt² (u = 0, g = 10, t = 2). s = 0 + ½×10×4 = 20 m. Answer: B. Trap: using g×t instead of ½g×t².

questions.stem: If an object has velocity-time graph as a straight line, what can be concluded?

options.option_text: Velocity is constant and acceleration is zero

questions.explanation: v-t straight line: slope = constant acceleration. If slope = 0 (horizontal), a = 0 (uniform motion). If sloped, a is constant. Answer: B (general case). Trap: confusing with A (only if horizontal line).

questions.stem: Two objects A and B start from the same point. A moves with constant velocity 5 m/s. B accelerates from rest at 2 m/s². After how many seconds will B catch up to A?
questions.explanation: A: s = 5t. B: s = ½×2×t² = t². When B catches A: t² = 5t. t² - 5t = 0. t(t - 5) = 0. t = 5 s (t = 0 is start). Answer: C. Trap: confusing displacement vs. velocity formulas.

questions.stem: A ball is thrown horizontally from a height of 20 m with initial velocity 10 m/s. What is the horizontal distance traveled before hitting the ground? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Vertical: h = ½gt². 20 = ½×10×t². t² = 4. t = 2 s. Horizontal: x = u×t = 10×2 = 20 m. Answer: C. Trap: mixing vertical and horizontal motions or forgetting to calculate time first.
